bib.title: Evaluating Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Evaluating Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey", Zishan Guo*, Renren Jin*, Chuang Liu* (equal contribution), Yufei Huang, Dan Shi, Supryadi, Linhao Yu, Yan Liu, Jiaxuan Li, Bojian Xiong, Deyi Xiong (corresponding). All authors, including the three first authors, are printed as Tianjin University. No venue is printed; the only identifier is "arXiv:2310.19736v3 [cs.CL] 25 Nov 2023", so it is a preprint, 2023.

COVERAGE: 111 of 111 pages extracted (347,283 chars), no faults.
- Pages 1-58 (the whole body, about 187k chars) were read in full, including Tables 1-6 and Figures 1-6.
- Pages 59-111 (references, 53 pages) were skimmed: I read pages 59-61 and 110-111 and keyword-scanned the rest.
- There are no appendices.

CLAIMS
- claim: The top-level taxonomy has three major groups: knowledge and capability, alignment, and safety. Two further sections cover specialized domains and evaluation organization.
  number: 3 groups (abstract); the body counts 5 domains
  setup: the authors' own framing, not derived from data
  quote: "We categorize the evaluation of LLMs into three major groups: knowledge and capability evaluation, alignment evaluation and safety evaluation." (p1); "evaluations encompassing these five fundamental domains and their respective subdomains" (p7)
  where: p1, p6-7
- claim: Each category is defined by its sub-areas (p7, p37, p46).
  - Knowledge and capability: question answering, knowledge completion, reasoning (commonsense, logical, multi-hop, mathematical), tool learning.
  - Alignment: ethics and morality, bias, toxicity, truthfulness.
  - Safety: robustness (prompt, task, alignment) and risk evaluation (LLM behaviours, LLMs as agents).
  - Specialized: biology and medicine, education, legislation, computer science, finance.
  - Organization: NLU/NLG benchmarks, knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, holistic benchmarks (leaderboards, arena).
  number: none
  quote: "robustness assessment that measures the stability of LLMs when confronted with disruptions, and risk evaluation that examines advanced / general-purpose LLMs behaviors and assesses them as agents" (p37)
- claim: Evaluation has shifted from task-centred to capability-centred benchmarks, often without training data, under zero- and few-shot settings.
  number: none
  quote: "marking a departure from traditional task-centered benchmarks to a focus on capability-centered assessments" (p4-5)
- claim: Static benchmarks have four stated problems: leakage into training data, a multiple-choice format that excludes open-ended questions, facts that go stale, and saturation.
  number: none
  quote: "it is easy for static evaluation datasets to be leaked and become training data for LLMs" (p56-57)
- claim: LLM judges are cheaper than humans but fallible.
  number: none
  quote: "Although advanced LLMs are more cost-efficient than humans, they could make mistakes about facts and take biases with their own preferences." (p57)
- claim: Scores alone give limited insight; the authors call for "enhancement-oriented" evaluation.
  number: none
  quote: "While the reported scores enable model comparison, the evaluations offer limited insights into LLMs." (p57)
- claim: Counts appear only in tables of other people's benchmarks. Table 5 lists 8 knowledge and reasoning benchmarks and Table 6 lists 10 holistic platforms (my row counts).
  number: 57 tasks, 15,908 instances for MMLU
  setup: Table 5, as reported by the benchmark authors
  quote: "MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) 57 English 15,908 Local" (p50)
- claim: One reported result illustrates agent difficulty.
  number: 10.59%
  setup: WebArena, best GPT-4-based agent, as reported by Zhou et al. 2023
  quote: "their best GPT-4-based (OpenAI, 2023) agent achieving a success rate of only 10.59%" (p41)
- claim: A cited audit found coreference bias benchmarks unreliable.
  number: 0%-58%
  setup: Blodgett et al. 2021 on WinoBias and Winogender
  quote: "only 0%–58% of the tests in these benchmarks are unaffected by these pitfalls" (p25)

LIMITS
- Catalogue only. There are no experiments, no meta-analysis and no new data. Section 7.2.2 "Evaluation Results" is a prose synthesis of other papers' findings.
- No selection method. It calls itself "a systematic literature review" (p5) but states no search strategy, inclusion criteria, date cutoff or count of papers reviewed. The only pointer is a GitHub list (tjunlp-lab/Awesome-LLMs-Evaluation-Papers).
- The authors concede the taxonomy "does not purport to comprehensively encompass the entirety of the evaluation landscape" (p8).
- Not covered: evaluating an application or system (as opposed to a model), offline versus online evaluation, regression suites, statistics and error bars, judge calibration. Human, automatic and LLM-based grading appear only in passing.
- Future directions (p56-57): risk, agent, dynamic and enhancement-oriented evaluation.
- Dated: models are GPT-3/3.5/4, Claude, Llama2; agent evaluation is called "in its infancy" (p41).
- Internal looseness: "three major groups" versus "five fundamental domains"; MMLU is described in prose as "57 additional subjects" (p49), while Table 5 gives 57 total.

BUILDS ON: Chang et al. (2023) and Liu et al. (2023i), which it says it "significantly extends" (p5). Chang is organised by tasks, datasets and methods; Liu focuses on alignment. Historical line: MUC (Grishman & Sundheim, 1996), SNLI (Bowman et al., 2015), SQuAD (Rajpurkar et al., 2016), GLUE and SuperGLUE (Wang et al., 2019b/a), MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021b), HELM (Liang et al., 2022). The "helpful, harmless, honest" framing is credited to Askell et al. (2021).

CODE: none.

FIGURES: Figure 1, p6, "Our proposed taxonomy of major categories and sub-categories of LLM evaluation." It is a single wheel showing all five branches and their sub-areas, quicker than the Section 2 prose. Its text extracts as scattered labels, so it would need an image crop.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean; a few words run together (p8, p14, p32). Figures 2-6 are tree diagrams that extract as flat lists.
- No embedded instructions found.
- Source typos: "Evaluation Harmness" for the lm-evaluation-harness (p53-54); footnotes 10 and 11 (Newcomb / EDT URLs) are swapped (p40); some citation suffixes differ between figures and text (for example EvalPlus is Liu 2023e in Figure 5 and 2023d on p45).
